name: Diani Beach Road Central
tagline: The main strip, with the coworking and the restaurants
description: The central stretch of the road running parallel to the beach, holding the restaurants, the supermarkets, the dive shops and the coworking spaces that gave Diani its small remote-work reputation. Accommodation ranges from apartments to villas, all a short walk from the sand.
bestFor: Anyone here to work remotely, with the coworking and the beach both close
pros: Coworking spaces and the best connectivity on the coast
Restaurants, supermarkets and dive shops on the strip
Beach access from almost anywhere along it
cons: Traffic and boda bodas on the main road

name: Galu Beach
tagline: The southern end, quieter and with the widest sand
description: The southern continuation of the beach towards Chale island, where the development thins out into villas and small hotels set back among the palms and the sand runs wide and largely empty. It is the calmest part of the coast here and about ten minutes from the strip.
bestFor: Stays that want the emptiest sand and are content to drive to the shops
pros: The widest and emptiest stretch of beach
Villas and quiet accommodation among the palms
Chale island and the southern reefs nearby
cons: Ten to fifteen minutes to the shops and restaurants
A vehicle or regular tuk-tuks are necessary

name: Ukunda
tagline: The town behind the beach, where Kenya actually lives
description: The town on the main Mombasa road a couple of kilometres inland, with the market, the matatu stage, the banks and the airstrip. It is an ordinary Kenyan town with none of the beach pricing, and it is where anyone staying long does their real shopping.
bestFor: Long stays wanting local prices and a town that has nothing to do with tourism
pros: Market and shops at genuine local prices
Rents a fraction of the beach road
The airstrip for flights to Nairobi

name: Tiwi Beach
tagline: The next bay north, undeveloped and much cheaper
description: A quieter beach a few kilometres north of Diani, with a fraction of the development, a reef close to shore and mostly self-catering cottages rather than hotels. It has been the budget alternative on this coast for decades and remains considerably cheaper.
bestFor: Longer stays wanting the same coast at a much lower price
pros: Reef close to shore for snorkelling
cons: Twenty minutes to Diani's shops and coworking
Very limited services and weak connectivity

name: Kaya Kinondo and the Inland Edge
tagline: Behind the beach, at the sacred forest
description: The area inland from the southern beaches around Kaya Kinondo, one of the sacred Mijikenda forests protected by local tradition and now UNESCO-listed, with village housing and a few eco-lodges. It is green, cool and completely removed from the beach economy.
bestFor: Stays that want the forest and village life rather than the beach strip
pros: The UNESCO-listed sacred forest and its guided walks
Cooler and shaded, away from the coast road
Very low costs and genuine village contact
cons: Fifteen to twenty minutes to the beach
Almost no services and slow internet
Transport is limited without a vehicle
